papers.title: Understanding teachers' curriculum reform receptivity: a psychological and cognitive perspective
papers.abstract: Purpose This study examined teachers' curriculum receptivity by integrating pedagogical beliefs, perceived benefits and costs, cognitive load and reform fatigue within a unified psychological framework. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative cross-sectional survey of 784 in-service teachers in the Teacher Professional Education (PPG) program was analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with bootstrapping to assess measurement validity and structural relationships. Findings Attitude was the strongest predictor of curriculum receptivity. Germane load had the largest positive effect on attitude and contributed to receptivity both directly and indirectly. Perceived benefits positively affect both attitude and receptivity, whereas reform fatigue has a negative effect. Intrinsic load had a small but significant positive effect on attitude and an indirect effect on receptivity, although its direct effect on receptivity was not significant. Pedagogical beliefs, perceived costs and extraneous load showed limited or non-significant effects. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional design limits causal interpretation, and the sample's concentration in Sulawesi may affect generalisability. This study contributes theoretically by treating curriculum receptivity as a psychologically mediated outcome and distinguishing the roles of different types of cognitive load. Practical implications Curriculum reform should promote meaningful teacher engagement through active learning, communicate benefits clearly and manage reform fatigue, rather than relying solely on reducing workload or changing beliefs. Originality/value This study offers an integrated model that highlights the central roles of attitude and productive cognitive engagement in shaping teachers' acceptance of curriculum reforms.

papers.title: Control of a ball balancing robot using a standalone reinforcement learning agent
papers.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to design and evaluate a standalone reinforcement learning (RL) controller for a ball-balancing robot (ballbot). Conventional linear controllers such as proportional integral derivative (PID) or linear quadratic regulator (LQR) require simplified models that neglect nonlinear couplings, whereas nonlinear methods such as nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) and sliding mode control impose high computational demands that hinder real-time implementation. These limitations make RL a necessary alternative, as it can directly learn robust control policies from interaction without explicit model simplification. Design/methodology/approach This study presents the development and training of a standalone RL controller to balance a ballbot using the deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG). In addition, twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) algorithm is included and used in training as a comparative baseline. A high-fidelity simulation environment is constructed using NVIDIA IsaacGym, which incorporates a custom computer-aided design (CAD) model and a physics-based simulation framework that facilitates agent training. Findings Both RL algorithms successfully learn to stabilize the ballbot. However, the DDPG-based controller demonstrates superior performance in maintaining balance under external disturbances and varying ground conditions. Robustness of the trained RL agent is validated through different testing scenarios including weight perturbation, external force application and movement over nonuniform ground surfaces. In addition, a comparison with a classical PID controller is presented to highlight relative strengths and limitations. Originality/value This research introduces a novel standalone RL controller designed specifically for the ballbot system, trained in a realistic and robust simulation environment. The study highlights the potential of RL-based strategies in managing the complexities of balancing tasks for inherently unstable robotic platforms. Further originality of this work lies in the design of a task-specific reward function that integrates penalties on tilt, angular velocity and lateral drift, ensuring that the RL agent learns robust, efficient balancing strategies beyond what standard reward formulations achieve.

papers.title: Parametric study on cushioning and energy absorption of density-Graded IWP and diamond triply periodic minimal surface lattice structures
papers.abstract: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) lattice structures are lightweight structures based on mathematical surfaces. They have been widely used in the field of additive manufacturing. In this study, single-morphology IWP and Diamond structures were designed using a parametric method. Based on the homogeneous structures, TPMS lattice structures with linear, cosine, and sinusoidal density gradients were further designed. Quasi-static compression experiments and numerical simulations were combined to systematically investigate the compressive deformation behavior, stress evolution, and energy absorption characteristics of the lattice structures under different topological configurations and density gradient distributions. The experimental and simulation results showed that all single-type structures exhibited a stress distribution with high stress at the upper and lower regions and low stress in the middle region. The Diamond structure showed better mechanical performance and energy absorption capability. It was more suitable for lightweight energy absorption applications. For the graded structures, the gradient stress of the IWP structures gradually decreased with decreasing density. In contrast, stress concentration was more likely to occur in low-density Diamond structures. Among all graded structures, the I-SIN structure showed the best overall performance. The D-COSINE structure exhibited the highest stiffness. The D-SIN structure demonstrated excellent load-bearing and energy absorption performance. For cylindrical configurations, the CY-D-SIN structure showed the best impact resistance. The overall performance of CY-Diamond structures was superior to that of CY-IWP structures. These structures can be adapted to different impact loading conditions.

papers.title: A comprehensive analysis of knee implants using finite element method to enhance biomechanical properties
papers.abstract: The increasing prevalence of knee joint disorders and the subsequent rise in knee implant surgeries have necessitated the development of innovative solutions to enhance biomechanical characteristics and overall performance. This research aims to analyze the mechanical performance of biocompatible materials for knee implants, focusing on their stress resistance, deformation behavior, and load distribution capabilities. Using finite element analysis (FEA), four materials—Ti-6Al-4V, SS 316L, Co-Cr-Mo, and ZrO2—were evaluated under flexion angles (0°, 15°, 40°, and 72°) and axial loads ranging from 600 N to 2500 N, replicating real-life conditions per ISO 14243-1 standards. Ti-6Al-4V exhibited the lowest stress levels across all angles, peaking at 28.52 MPa at 40°, indicating superior stress resistance. ZrO2 displayed the highest contact pressures (25.73 MPa at 0°), reflecting excellent load distribution capabilities, but also registered the highest stress (30.63 MPa at 40°). SS 316L demonstrated balanced performance, with moderate stress and deformation levels, while Co-Cr-Mo showed robust contact pressure but higher stress susceptibility under extreme loads. Ti-6Al-4V emerged as the most resilient material, combining low deformation and consistent stress resistance, making it ideal for high-performance applications. These findings emphasize the importance of material selection in knee implant design, advancing the development of durable and efficient orthopedic solutions.

papers.title: Advances in Metallic Fixation Materials for Bone Fracture Fixation: A Review
papers.abstract: Metallic biomaterials remain central to bone fracture fixation because they provide the mechanical stability required to maintain alignment and support healing under physiological loading. This review examines conventional surgical metals, including stainless steel (SS), cobalt–chromium (Co–Cr) alloys, and titanium (Ti) and its alloys, together with emerging resorbable metals based on magnesium (Mg), iron (Fe), and zinc (Zn). SS remains widely used because of its strength, low cost, and established clinical history, although its high elastic modulus, corrosion-related ion release, limited osseointegration, and susceptibility to infection are limitations. Co–Cr alloys provide superior strength, hardness, wear resistance, and corrosion resistance, but their high stiffness and potential release of Co and Cr species restrict fracture-fixation applications. Ti alloys offer a favorable combination of low density, corrosion resistance, biocompatibility, and a lower elastic modulus than SS and Co–Cr, although stress shielding, implant-associated infection, and concerns regarding alloying-element release persist. Resorbable Mg-, Fe-, and Zn-based systems seek to provide temporary mechanical support while gradually transferring load to regenerating bone thus eliminating implant-removal surgery. However, rapid Mg degradation, slow Fe resorption, and the limited intrinsic strength of Zn remain barriers to clinical translation. Alloying, controlled porosity, additive manufacturing, thermomechanical processing, and surface modification can improve mechanical, degradation, osseointegration, and antibacterial performance, but may introduce concerns involving fatigue resistance, localized corrosion, ion release, manufacturing complexity, and long-term safety. Future development should prioritize synchronization of mechanical retention and degradation with bone healing, together with standardized long-term in vivo evaluation of corrosion products, biological responses, and fixation performance.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Assisted Multi-Objective Optimization of 2D Elastodynamic Metamaterials: Pareto Analysis, Algorithmic Comparison, and Robustness Assessment
papers.abstract: The design of 2D elastodynamic metamaterials requires navigating complex, high dimensional spaces to balance competing functional objectives, such as minimizing bandgap location while maximizing bandgap width.Traditional finite element analysis (FEA) is computationally prohibitive for vast design spaces, and current data-driven optimization studies frequently overlook the empirical variability of simulation data, risking the selection of statistical artifacts.This study presents a catalogue-constrained, machine learningassisted multi-objective optimization (ML-MOO) framework utilizing a dataset of 1,400 unique binary metamaterial geometries.We developed an Extra Trees surrogate model and compared six optimization algorithms (Bayesian Optimization, PSO, Differential Evolution, MOEA, GA, and NSGA-II).Results indicate that MOEA, BO, PSO, and DE converge on an identical global best utility (0.8176), with MOEA demonstrating superior sample efficiency.The optimized designs achieved up to a 547.7% increase in bandgap width compared to the dataset baseline, albeit with a 9.8% increase in central frequency, illustrating the inherent physical trade-off.Crucially, a robustness assessment revealed that all 52 global Pareto optimal geometries are singletons lacking repeated observations, while replicated geometries exhibited high empirical variability (Coefficient of Variation up to 173% for bandgap width).This highlights a critical distinction between computational optimization performance and empirical reproducibility.The study concludes by proposing a conservative 12-point engineering shortlist and advocating for future robustness aware optimization frameworks that incorporate variance penalties to ensure physically reliable metamaterial designs.

papers.title: Tear Arc Size Was Not Associated With 10‐Year Outcomes After Hip Labral Repair, Yet Higher Number of Anchors Was Associated With Lower Outcomes
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: To assess the effect of the tear size and number of anchors on patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) and incidence of revision surgery or conversion to total hip arthroplasty for patients undergoing hip arthroscopy at a minimum 10-year follow-up. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted of patients undergoing primary hip arthroscopic labral repair between January 2011 and December 2014 at a single academic institution. Patients with revision procedures, prior ipsilateral hip surgery, labral debridement, or <10-year follow-up were excluded. The tear arc size and number of anchors were recorded from operative reports. PROMs included modified Harris Hip Score, Hip Outcome Score-Activities of Daily Living (HOS-ADL), HOS-Sports, Tegner, visual analog score, and satisfaction (0-10). Associations between the number of anchors and tear size with PROMs were assessed with univariate and multivariate linear regression. Multivariate logistic regression was used to evaluate the predictors of reoperation or conversion to total hip arthroplasty. RESULTS: Seventy-three hips were included (mean age: 36.2 ± 10.8 years; 72.6% women) with a mean follow-up of 10.9 ± 0.7 years (range: 10.0-13.0). At ≥10 years, the mean modified Harris Hip Score was 79.6 ± 17.2, HOS-ADL 83.4 ± 17.1, HOS-Sports 72.8 ± 25.5, Tegner 3.8 ± 1.5, visual analog score 2.4 ± 2.7 (rest) and 2.7 ± 2.7 (use), and satisfaction 8.5 ± 2.4. Tear arc was not associated with any PROMs on regression analysis. In multivariable analysis, each additional anchor was associated with lower HOS-ADL (β = -5.6, P = .048) and HOS-Sports (β = -8.5, P = .044) and higher visual analog score pain at rest (β = 0.8, P = .048). Patient-acceptable symptom state was achieved by 60.3% of patients for modified Harris Hip Score, 49.3% for HOS-ADL, and 76.7% for HOS-Sports. No statistically significant association was detected between sex, anchor number, or tear arc size and subsequent surgery. CONCLUSIONS: At minimum 10 years after arthroscopic labral repair, tear arc size was not associated with PROMs, and satisfactory PROMs and high patient-acceptable symptom state achievement rates were observed. A higher anchor number was associated with modestly lower PROMs. Subsequent surgery was not associated with sex, anchor number, or tear arc size. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, retrospective cohort study.

papers.title: A Bayesian neural network digital twin prototype trained on finite element and monitoring data for earthfill dam monitoring
papers.abstract: Interpreting dam monitoring records together with numerical models is difficult for earthfill dams, where seepage, deformation and seismic loading interact. This study develops a digital twin prototype for the Houzian Dam, western Iran, based on a Bayesian neural network (BNN) trained on finite element (FE) simulations and field monitoring records. The database combines 4,862 monitoring records (2013–2025) from five piezometers and three settlement gauges, cyclic triaxial test results and FE-generated responses. The calibrated FE model reached R 2 of at least 0.95 and relative errors of at most 6.8% at the three representative piezometers. On a randomly partitioned test set, the BNN gave an RMSE of 0.087 and an R 2 of 0.984 on normalised variables after sequential updating; before updating, the RMSE was 0.137, higher than that of a Transformer baseline (0.128). The updating status of the baselines is not reported. Sequential assimilation reduced the average predictive variance from 0.021 to 0.008 and the RMSE by 36.5%. Physical knowledge enters only through FE-generated data and laboratory-derived properties, not through governing-equation residuals. Seismic results are exploratory, and interval calibration and ablation analyses were not performed.

papers.title: Predictors and an exploratory nomogram for conversion to total hip arthroplasty after acetabular posterior wall fractures fixation
papers.abstract: This study aimed to identify predictors and develop a nomogram for predicting conversion to total hip arthroplasty (THA) following open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) of acetabular strike-type posterior wall (PW) fractures. A retrospective analysis included 194 patients (195 hips) treated operatively between 2015 and 2020. Demographic, perioperative, and imaging data were analyzed. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors, and a nomogram was constructed using R software. The conversion rate to THA was 15.4% (30/195), with a mean conversion time of 21.7 months. Multivariable analysis identified age > 39.5 years (OR = 4.10; P = 0.008), higher BMI (OR = 1.16; P = 0.030), delayed surgery (OR = 1.14/day; P = 0.014), posterior dislocation (OR = 4.51; P = 0.009), and femoral head lesions (OR = 4.78; P = 0.001) as independent predictors. The nomogram demonstrated strong predictive accuracy (C-index = 0.84, AUC = 0.84) and clinical utility via decision curve analysis. Over 70% of conversions occurred within two years post-ORIF. These findings highlight the importance of early intervention, weight management, and addressing dislocation/head injuries. The exploratory nomogram may help clinicians consider alternative interventions for high-risk patients.

papers.title: Postmenopausal steroid conditions enable physiologically relevant 3D bioprinting of ER+ breast cancer
papers.abstract: The tumour microenvironment is increasingly recognised as a complex and dynamic system in which tumour epithelial cells interact with host-derived factors to influence cancer progression. Conventional models, including xenografts and patient-derived organoids, only partially recapitulate this complexity. In particular, the contribution of the steroid microenvironment, a critical regulator in endocrine-related cancers such as breast cancer, remains insufficiently modelled. Herein, we emphasise the importance of replicating the human endocrine environment for successful 3D cell propagation and demonstrate the potential of high-content bioprinting to generate primary breast tumour models that closely mimic native histology. Using a 3D bioprinting approach that utilises mammalian derived constituents and additives, we modify the steroid environment to replicate the alterations in steroidogenesis that arise in post-menopausal breast cancer patients. These bioprinted models were characterised using high-resolution imaging, immunohistochemistry, and viability assays to assess structural organisation and cellular function. Application of this approach to primary estrogen receptor-positive (ER + ) breast tumours enabled sustained propagation over a two-week period, with retention of key histological features closely resembling the original tumour architecture. Furthermore, conditioned media derived from tumour-associated breast adipose tissue was used to model local steroidogenic activity in vitro, revealing differential effects on tumour cell viability. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that incorporation of a physiologically relevant steroid microenvironment enhances the fidelity of 3D breast cancer models. This platform provides a versatile tool for investigating endocrine–tumour interactions and may support the development of more predictive models for studying hormone-driven breast cancer progression and therapeutic response.

papers.title: Association of dislocation and patient-reported improvements after total hip arthroplasty: a multicenter registry-based study of 4,725 patients
papers.abstract: Background and purpose: The impact of dislocation on patient-reported improvements after total hip arthroplasty (THA) is largely unknown. We aimed to analyze the association between dislocation treated with closed reduction and patient-reported improvements from baseline to 12 months after primary THA.Methods: This population-based cohort study included 5,102 primary THAs in 4,725 patients due to primary osteoarthritis performed at 3 Danish departments from 2019 to 2024. Early dislocation was the primary exposure, defined as a first-time dislocation within 3 months after surgery, whereas late dislocation was defined as a first-time dislocation 3 to 12 months after surgery. Dislocations were identified using the Danish Hip Arthroplasty Register (DHR). Oxford Hip Scores (OHSs) were collected preoperatively and 3, 12, and 24 months after the primary THA. Marginal mean differences (MMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using multilevel Tobit regression and adjusted for age, sex, and Charlson comorbidity index obtained from the DHR.Results: The incidence of early dislocation was 2.5% (125/5,102), whereas it was 0.5% (24/5,102) for late dislocation. After 12 months, patients with an early dislocation had an adjusted OHS improvement of 18.1 (CI 16.1–20.1), compared with 22.5 (CI 22.2–22.8) in patients without a dislocation, corresponding to an adjusted difference in OHS improvement of –4.4 (CI –6.4 to –2.4). For late dislocation, the adjusted difference in OHS improvement was –1.2 (CI –6.0 to 3.6).Conclusion: Early dislocation treated with closed reduction was associated with smaller patient-reported improvements 12 months after THA compared with no dislocation. This difference was just below the minimal important difference, but a clinically relevant association could not be excluded. Estimates for late dislocation were imprecise. These findings support continued efforts to prevent dislocation.

papers.title: From vascular failure to biological repair: Mesenchymal stem cell strategies in osteonecrosis of the femoral head
papers.abstract: Osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) is a debilitating orthopedic condition that predominantly affects young adults. Interruption in the normal flow of the terminal vascular supply of the femoral head leads to bone cell death, trabecular collapse, and secondary osteoarthritis. Current therapies, such as total hip arthroplasty (THA), bisphosphonates, and core decompression (CD), provide partial disease change. These do not treat the underlying biological deficiencies that cause progression. Growing evidence suggests that ONFH develops through two closely linked processes. A failure of the local blood supply and loss of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) within the bone marrow niche. This review discusses mechanistic, preclinical, and clinical evidence published between 2020 and 2026 on MSC-based therapies for ONFH. MSCs release factors that help form new blood vessels through VEGF and angiopoietins. They also support bone formation through RUNX2-mediated differentiation. At the same time, IGF-1 and HGF help protect cells from apoptosis. Meta-analyses suggest that stem cell-augmented CD may reduce femoral head collapse and, as a result, lower the need for THA. MSC-derived exosomes are also gaining attention as a cell-free option. However, their clinical translation is still hampered by a number of issues, such as donor-related variability, a lack of established protocols, a lack of extended follow-ups, and regulatory restrictions. Larger multicenter trials, GMP-compliant production, and ongoing research on MSCs modified at the genetic level, allogeneic platforms, and mechanotransduction-based strategies will all be necessary for future advancements.

papers.title: Computational-experimental investigation of heterogeneous sheet-based TPMS lattice scaffolds fabricated by fused filament fabrication for bone-mimetic applications
papers.abstract: Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) lattice structures have attracted significant interest in bone tissue engineering because of their interconnected porous architecture and favorable mechanical properties. However, previous studies have primarily focused on individual TPMS topologies or experimental characterization, with limited investigation of validated finite element analysis (FEA) frameworks for heterogeneous sheet-based TPMS lattices at constant relative density. This study develops and experimentally validates a unified computational-experimental framework for predicting the compressive behavior and stress distribution of homogeneous and heterogeneous TPMS lattice structures fabricated using fused filament fabrication (FFF). Sixteen sheet-based TPMS architectures, comprising four homogeneous and twelve heterogeneous configurations based on Primitive, Gyroid, Double Diamond, and Diamond unit cells, were systematically designed at a constant relative density of 30%. Nonlinear FEA using a multilinear isotropic hardening material model predicted the compressive response and von Mises stress distribution, followed by quasi-static compression testing for validation. The numerical predictions showed good agreement with the experimental results, confirming the reliability of the proposed modeling framework. Quantitative analysis further revealed that discrepancies between predicted and measured mechanical properties were primarily caused by manufacturing-induced porosity variations inherent to the FFF process. The validated predictive framework provides a scientific basis for the mechanics-informed design and optimization of architected lattice biomaterials and other lightweight cellular structures with tunable mechanical performance.

papers.title: Intelligent Inverse Design of High-Flux Acoustic Metamaterials for Aviation Power Systems
papers.abstract: There is a contradiction between high ventilation capacity and low and medium frequency noise reduction in the confined space of the aviation power and environmental control system. This paper proposes a reverse design framework. The framework combines deep agent model with heuristic algorithm. The framework uses a multi-layer perceptron ( MLP ) to construct an acoustic surrogate model. It reaches a high determination coefficient ( R2 ) of 0.9969 when predicting the first resonance peak frequency. Physical constraints such as wall thickness and manufacturing tolerances are incorporated into the genetic algorithm ( GA ). In this paper, a bottom-up sequential cascade optimization strategy is established. In this paper, a three-layer labyrinth acoustic metamaterial with an outer diameter of 100 mm and a ventilation rate of 16 % is designed by this strategy. The finite element simulation verifies its excellent isolation performance for discrete line spectrum noise at 680 Hz, 1150 Hz and 1550 Hz. The peak sound transmission loss ( STL ) reaches 43 dB. The mechanism analysis shows that the interlayer impedance transition and near-field interference effect significantly enhance the global acoustic attenuation characteristics of the structure. Further extended analysis considers the 25 % limit ventilation rate. The analysis verifies the applicability and robustness of the framework under strong aerodynamic flow constraints. It provides an effective way for aeroacoustic structure optimization. Aeroacoustic structure optimization needs to take into account both ventilation capacity and manufacturability.

papers.title: AI surrogate modeling for real-time tokamak equilibrium prediction: benchmarking neural architectures and validation on EXL-50U
papers.abstract: Fast and reliable plasma equilibrium prediction is essential for real-time tokamak operation, control, and fusion applications. However, conventional numerical solutions of the Grad–Shafranov (GS) equation are often too computationally expensive for real-time deployment. To address this challenge, we develop an artificial intelligence (AI) surrogate framework and systematically evaluate five representative architectures, namely the multilayer perceptron (MLP), the convolutional neural network (CNN), the Fourier neural operator (FNO), the Transformer, and the Kolmogorov–Arnold network (KAN), using a numerically generated GS equilibrium database comprising 100,000 independent and identically distributed (IID) samples and 10,000 out-of-distribution (OOD) samples. Under a unified protocol, we assess prediction accuracy, inference efficiency, model scaling, and robustness under both IID and OOD conditions. We further establish a device-level validation chain on the EXL-50U tokamak by linking GS numerical solutions, surrogate predictions, and the standard Shape Editor solver reference, thereby explicitly evaluating simulation-to-device consistency. The surrogate models achieve errors of 10⁻³–10⁻² relative to GS solutions, while the discrepancy between GS solutions and the device reference remains at the 10⁻³ level. Transformer achieves the highest IID accuracy, whereas CNN provides a favorable balance between prediction accuracy, robustness, and inference efficiency, with a TensorRT latency of 0.7 ms. OOD experiments across unseen plasma geometries and parameter regimes reveal substantial architecture-dependent differences: CNN and FNO maintain superior extrapolation stability (relative L2 error = 4%–5%), while architectures with weaker inductive biases exhibit greater performance degradation. Scaling experiments further show that increasing dataset size and model capacity consistently improves interpolation accuracy but does not necessarily enhance extrapolation, indicating a trade-off between model capacity and OOD generalization. Overall, this work establishes a systematic benchmarking and device-consistent validation framework for AI-based GS equilibrium prediction. The results demonstrate the potential of data-driven surrogates for real-time tokamak operation and provide practical guidance for selecting reliable architectures for future plasma control and fusion applications.

Sobol sensitivity analysis quantitatively revealed the dominant precursor factors and their interactive effects on QY, providing mechanistic understanding of boron doping. Under the optimized precursor mass ratio, the as-prepared B-CDs achieved a QY of 51.84%. The material was characterized by UV–Vis spectroscopy, FTIR, XRD, XPS, TEM, Raman spectroscopy and Zeta potential. Investigation of the quenching process of CrO-B-CDs revealed that the quenching behavior is attributed to static quenching mainly induced by oxidation of surface hydroxyl groups, demonstrating that abundant surface hydroxyl groups are the key fluorescence source of B-CDs. Benefiting from this surface-quenching effect triggered by potassium dichromate, a CrO-B-CD “off–on” fluorescent nanoprobe was fabricated for glutathione detection. The sensor exhibited a linear detection range of 0–16.0 μM (R2 = 0.997) and a limit of detection as low as 24.0 nM at pH 6.0 with a reaction time of 2 min. Satisfactory recoveries were obtained for GSH quantification in human serum samples. Moreover, B-CDs displayed favorable biocompatibility and excellent photostability, enabling effective fluorescence imaging in HeLa cells. papers.title: Mapping the use of LEGO® serious play® in health professions education: a scoping review of educational outcomes and applications
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: (LSP) method has been developed as an innovative pedagogical strategy in higher education, particularly in health professions education, where its use has been associated with active learning, reflection, and engagement. However, gaps remain in the understanding of how it has been applied and of its main educational outcomes. This review aimed to map the use of LSP in health professions education, identifying its applications, contexts, and outcomes. METHODS: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and the PRISMA-ScR checklist, with searches performed in electronic databases including PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, EBSCO, and Google Scholar. Studies addressing the use of LSP in health-related higher education were independently selected by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer when consensus could not be reached. Data were extracted and analysed using descriptive and thematic approaches. RESULTS: Nine studies were included: six qualitative studies (66.7%), two quantitative studies (22.2%), and one experience report (11.1%). The studies were conducted across different contexts in health professions education. The thematic analysis identified five main categories: (1) promotion of engagement and active learning; (2) development of critical-reflective thinking; (3) construction of professional identity and socio-emotional competencies; (4) mediation of sociocultural processes; and (5) interprofessional collaboration. Overall, the studies reported perceived educational benefits of LSP, particularly in student engagement, depth of reflection, and collaborative learning. CONCLUSIONS: has been used in health professions education as a pedagogical strategy associated with student engagement, reflection, professional identity development, socio-emotional competencies, and interprofessional collaboration. Although the current evidence base is heterogeneous and predominantly qualitative, its applicability is shown across different contexts, interprofessional settings, and educational environments. Future research should consider comparative and longitudinal designs, report implementation fidelity more clearly, and examine whether reported educational benefits are sustained beyond the immediate novelty of the intervention.

papers.title: Proximal policy optimization with adaptive fuzzy logic (PPO-AFL) for high-efficiency maximum power point tracking in three-phase grid-connected photovoltaic systems
papers.abstract: In this work, a new controller called Proximal Policy Optimization with Adaptive Fuzzy Logic (PPO-AFL) is introduced for Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) in a 4.98 kW three-phase grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) system. All testing was done through MATLAB R2023b/Simulink. The PPO-AFL controller links a PPO reinforcement learning agent with Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE) to a two-timescale Takagi-Sugeno-Kang (TSK) Adaptive Fuzzy Logic (AFL) unit. This setup adjusts the fuzzy membership function parameters in real time without needing any labelled training data. A combined reward signal simultaneously addresses maximum-power extraction, DC-link voltage regulation, grid-current harmonic distortion, and duty-cycle smoothness. The grid-side terms are evaluated against selected harmonic-distortion and power-factor criteria used as power-quality reference limits; full IEEE 1547–2018 compliance is not claimed. Under idealized MATLAB/Simulink simulation conditions, results indicate a steady-state tracking efficiency of 99.5%, a settling time of 52 ms, a power ripple of ± 3 W, a grid current THD of 0.8%, and a power factor of 0.998. These values are better than ten reference algorithms including P&O (92.1%), INC (93.6%), ANN-MPPT (97.3%), and DDPG-MPPT (97.9%) across all measured criteria. An ablation study with five system variants confirms that each component adds independently to the final performance. Statistical tests across 150 simulation runs per algorithm (1,650 observations across the eleven methods; one-way ANOVA, F(10, 1639) = 1124.7, p < 0.001) confirm the findings are significant. Hardware tests such as HIL, PIL, and DSP/FPGA prototype work are needed in future to verify these results in real conditions.

papers.title: Evaluation of a Multifaceted Redesign of an Asynchronous Pharmacy Calculations Course
papers.abstract: Pharmaceutical calculations is an essential competency for student pharmacists, yet pharmacy educators continue to identify challenges in teaching and assessing calculation skills. At Western University of Health Sciences (WesternU), performance in a longitudinal asynchronous pharmacy calculations course declined across consecutive cohorts, prompting a multifaceted curriculum redesign. The primary objective was to evaluate longitudinal trends in student performance in a first-year pharmacy calculations course and describe performance following implementation of a multifaceted curriculum redesign. A secondary objective was to examine associations between pre-admission academic characteristics and final examination performance. Final examination performance and selected pre-admission academic characteristics were analyzed using nonparametric comparisons including Kruskal–Wallis, Mann–Whitney U tests, Spearman correlations, and linear regression. Mean raw final examination performance declined from 88.7% in 2020 to 75.8% in 2023 and increased to 81.3% in 2024 following implementation of the curriculum redesign. The overall comparison was statistically significant (p < 0.001). Apart from undergraduate study type, pre-admission academic characteristics demonstrated weak to modest associations with final examination performance; math Grade Point Average (GPA) had the strongest association (Spearman ρ = 0.297, p < 0.001). Student performance increased in the first cohort following implementation of a multifaceted redesign of an asynchronous pharmacy calculations course. Findings support continued evaluation of structured practice, active learning, and assessment opportunities in pharmacy calculations education.

papers.title: Closed-Loop CFD-Driven Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization of an Opposing Jet in Supersonic Flow for a Blunt Body
papers.abstract: This study develops an automated closed-loop CFD-driven multi-objective Bayesian optimization workflow for a blunt body in supersonic flow. The workflow integrates ParEGO-based adaptive sampling and Gaussian-process surrogates with automated transient CFD execution, heat-flux stability assessment, and metric extraction. During adaptive sampling, the scalar surrogate is updated using the accepted CFD results and guides selection of the next operating condition. The normalized bow-shock and Mach-disk locations predicted by the numerical method differed from the nitrogen experimental values by 5.5% and 8.7%, respectively. Leave-one-out cross-validation of the surrogates trained on the final optimization dataset yielded R2 values of 0.9544 and 0.9744 and NRMSE values of 6.03% and 4.86% for the cooling- and drag-reduction-benefit objectives, respectively. Late-stage hypervolume gains of 0.10–0.27% indicated little marginal improvement within the available budget. Analysis of the resulting solution set identified jet total temperature and total-pressure ratio as the variables most strongly associated with cooling and drag-reduction benefits, respectively, while preference analysis mapped parameter ranges to cooling-, drag-reduction-, and balanced-priority designs. The proposed workflow provides an integrated and reproducible route from sequential CFD evaluation to preference-dependent opposing-jet design under a limited computational budget.

papers.title: Beyond Reduced-Order Models: Energy-Based Transient Stability Assessment of Current-Limited Grid-Forming Inverters
papers.abstract: This repository provides the computational framework, simulation models, numerical results, and supporting research material associated with the study Beyond Reduced-Order Models: Energy-Based Transient Stability Assessment of Current-Limited Grid-Forming Inverters. The research investigates the applicability of reduced-order dynamic models and Lyapunov-based stability certificates to grid-forming (GFM) inverters operating under current-limiting conditions, with particular emphasis on structural model uncertainty, post-fault recovery dynamics, and critical clearing time (CCT) assessment. Research scope and methodology The computational framework combines nonlinear power system dynamics, energy-based stability analysis, electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulations, and non-parametric uncertainty quantification inspired by the Best Estimate Plus Uncertainty (BEPU) methodology used in nuclear safety analysis. The main research activities include: Implementation of reduced-order switched dynamic models of GFM inverters. State-dependent switched (SdS) Lyapunov energy functions and region-of-attraction estimation. Detailed electromagnetic transient models incorporating cascaded voltage and current controllers, digital control, LC filters, current saturation, and anti-windup strategies. Comparative assessment of circular current limiting and enhanced virtual impedance (EVI) limiting. Critical clearing time estimation under parametric and operating-condition uncertainties. Statistical tolerance limits using Wilks’ order statistics and exact binomial inference. Characterisation of structural model discrepancies through post-fault power mismatch and Lyapunov energy injection. Development and assessment of a composite EMT–energy-based procedure for transient stability evaluation. Investigation of model applicability as a function of short-circuit ratio (SCR), controller design, and network operating conditions. Computational efficiency assessment and independent statistical validation. Test systems Two power system configurations are investigated: A single grid-forming inverter connected to an infinite bus, evaluated across different grid strengths, impedance characteristics, operating conditions, and controller configurations. A modified WSCC 9-bus system incorporating two grid-forming inverters and one synchronous generator, enabling the investigation of multi-converter interactions, network contingencies, and local grid-strength effects. Computational environment and research material The research material includes Python scripts, MATLAB/Simulink and Simscape Electrical models, simulation parameters, uncertainty sampling configurations, numerical datasets, statistical calculations, and figure-generation routines. The simulations encompass reduced-order models, continuous dq representations, averaged EMT models, and selected switching-level PWM simulations. The repository is intended to support the reproducibility, independent verification, and further development of the numerical experiments and mathematical methodology presented in the associated manuscript. Scientific contribution and potential applications The central contribution is the characterisation of the loss of transferability of reduced-order stability guarantees to higher-fidelity models when internal converter dynamics become relevant during fault recovery. The framework provides a basis for further research into model-fidelity assessment, uncertainty-aware transient stability analysis, grid-forming converter design, renewable energy and battery energy storage system integration, and protection clearing-time requirements. The reported guarantees are conditional on the specified uncertainty distributions, controller families, model assumptions, and stability criteria. A general deterministic transfer of reduced-order Lyapunov certificates to EMT models is not claimed.

papers.title: A Vis-NIR penetrometer system for in-situ soil carbon stock estimation using cumulative mass coordinates
papers.abstract: In-situ measurement of soil organic carbon (SOC) using visible and near-infrared (Vis-NIR) spectroscopy offers the advantage of being rapid, non-destructive, and cost-effective. However, measuring SOC stocks throughout the soil profile remains challenging due to the difficulty of acquiring continuous depth information without excavating the profile. This study evaluated the effectiveness of a Vis-NIR penetrometer system in predicting SOC concentration, bulk density (BD), and SOC stock up to one metre in-situ . Two low-cost spectrometers were used to acquire the reflectance spectra across 350–2200 nm during penetration, and a moisture sensor was installed at the tip of the penetrometer to estimate soil moisture. A field study was conducted on a farm in eastern Australia with 19 cores, comprising 172 soil samples. Soil samples were analysed for their SOC and BD at 10 cm intervals and corresponded to spectral measurements. During modelling, a leave-one-core-out cross-validation was carried out, and a foundation model, Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN), was compared to partial least squares regression (PLSR) and Cubist. SOC stock was predicted with good predictive performance (R 2 = 0.73, concordance correlation coefficient = 0.85) by TabPFN, which consistently outperformed PLSR and Cubist. Additionally, predicting SOC stock without predicting BD yielded the same level of accuracy because of the high correlation between SOC concentration and SOC stock. Uncertainty quantification by TabPFN also provided reasonable coverage for observed values. However, the mean prediction interval width was still large, indicating room for further improvement. High-resolution sampling using spectral methods also enabled SOC stock calculation using the equivalent soil mass approach. This study demonstrated the potential of a Vis-NIR penetrometer system that can perform in-situ estimation of SOC stock. Further field testing across a range of soil types, moisture conditions, and management systems is needed to validate the performance and broader applicability of the system.

papers.title: Quantifying Macromolecular Transport and Retention Kinetics of Folate-Targeted Polymers in Breast Cancer: A Physics-Informed Differentiable Digital Twin Approach
papers.abstract: Accurate characterization of targeted nanomedicine transport kinetics remains a challenge in cancer therapeutics due to sparse, noisy experimental biodistribution data. Conventional models separate simulation from parameter estimation and often fail to capture the multiphase uptake and prolonged matrix retention of targeted macromolecular carriers within the tumor microenvironment. Here, we present a physics-informed neural network (PINN) architecture serving as a continuous gray-box tool, a differentiable digital twin (DT), to address parameter identifiability challenges in cancer nanomedicine kinetics. The framework integrates a reduced-order phenomenological physical prior with Deep Galerkin Method (DGM) layers, residual-based attention, and self-adaptive loss scaling to ensure optimization stability while preserving structural mass balances. Validated on an ultrasparse, eight-point murine breast cancer biodistribution dataset of folate-targeted poly(styrene-alt-maleic anhydride)–paclitaxel nanoparticles (FA–PSMAC–PTX), the differentiable DT reconstructed continuous concentration profiles with high in-sample fidelity (R2 > 0.98, RMSE ≈ 12 μg mL–1) and predicted withheld time points out of sample (leave-one-time-point-out Rcv2 = 0.74) and resolved hidden transport constants. Information-theoretic comparisons of the mechanistic structures indicated improved parsimony over passive diffusion baselines. Furthermore, the autograd-preserving framework yields instant analytical dose-sensitivity fields (∂Ĉt/∂C0) detailing real-time tumor exposure changes. This framework provides an interpretable method for profiling the real-world kinetics of complex polymer conjugates in solid oncology models, bridging computational data science and rational nanomedicine design.

papers.title: Molecular-level siloxane coating on nanoporous anatase TiO2 for controlled Au nanoparticle deposition
papers.abstract: Titania aerogels composed of anatase nanocrystals are promising catalyst supports owing to their high surface area and porosity; however, their practical application is limited by structural collapse of the TiO 2 gels during the drying process, as well as aggregation of the supported metal nanoparticles. Herein, we report a surface sol–gel strategy for constructing nanometer-thick nanoporous coatings on monolithic TiO 2 aerogels using cage siloxanes as the molecular building blocks. papers.title: Bayesian-Optimized ANN for Predicting the Thermodynamic and Exergy Performance of an Automobile HVAC Compressor Using R1234yf
papers.abstract: Compressors are the most energy-consuming components of automobile heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems. Thus, compressor performance mapping and accurate predictions are vital for enhancing the energy efficiency of these systems. In this work, an artificial neural network (ANN) model with Bayesian optimization was employed to predict the thermodynamic and exergetic performance of a 160 cm3 fixed-displacement swash-plate compressor using R1234yf as the refrigerant. For modeling, 2574 experimental samples were obtained under different operating conditions, using compressor speed, indoor air temperature, indoor airflow rate, outdoor air velocity, and the measured suction state (temperature, pressure, specific volume, enthalpy, and entropy) as inputs, and were randomly split into training, validation, and test subsets (65/15/20%), stratified by compressor speed. With the considered input parameters, the refrigerant mass flow rate, discharge pressure, pressure ratio, discharge temperature, compressor power (electrical and refrigerant sides), volumetric efficiency, isentropic efficiency, overall efficiency, compressor exergy destruction, and exergy efficiency were predicted. Initially, Bayesian optimization was used to determine the ANN architecture and training parameters, followed by hyperparameter sensitivity, training and validation loss, residual distribution, and prediction error analyses. The optimized ANN provided coefficient of determination (R2) values above 0.95 for all parameters except overall efficiency (0.82), while the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) did not exceed 1.65% for all predictions (independent test subset). The highest accuracy was obtained for electrical compressor power, with an R2 of 0.9998 and MAPE of 0.29%. The predictions of refrigerant mass flow rate, pressure ratio, compressor exergy destruction, and exergy efficiency also showed very good agreement with the experimental results, with R2 values of 0.9988, 0.9991, 0.9994, and 0.9891, respectively. Volumetric efficiency was predicted more accurately than isentropic and overall efficiencies, with an R2 of 0.9974 and MAPE of 0.59%. Grouped five-fold cross-validation by operating condition reduced the mean R2 from 0.977 to 0.807, and overall efficiency (R2 = −0.11) did not generalize to unseen conditions. The results demonstrate the capability of the optimized ANN to predict the investigated compressor performance parameters within the experimental operating domain. However, the model was developed for a specific 160 cm3 swash plate compressor configuration under a fixed refrigerant charge and thermostatic expansion valve setting. Therefore, its applicability to other compressor configurations, refrigerant charge levels, thermostatic expansion valve settings, and operating conditions beyond the investigated experimental ranges requires further experimental validation.

papers.title: Digital Twins and Drug Development
papers.abstract: Digital twins are data-driven virtual representations that enable the dynamic modeling of biological systems, patient-specific data, and medical devices. This review discusses the applications of digital twins in nuclear medicine and drug development. In drug development, digital twins may support the translation of preclinical findings to human physiology using data from platforms such as organ-on-a-chip systems, allowing the efficacy, biodistribution, and toxicity of candidate molecules to be assessed at an earlier stage and potentially reducing the need for animal experiments. In nuclear medicine, the integration of anatomical, functional, and pharmacokinetic data within a common modeling environment may offer new opportunities for personalized dosimetry and treatment planning. In radiopharmaceutical therapies such as [ 177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE and [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA, the combined use of physiologically based pharmacokinetic models, patient-specific imaging data, and Monte Carlo-based dose calculations may contribute to a more individualized assessment of treatment response and normal tissue toxicity. Instrumentation digital twins for positron emission tomography and single-photon emission computed tomography systems also represent a developing research area for system design, image reconstruction, quality control, and protocol optimization. In some applications, the absence of continuous bidirectional data exchange between the physical system and the model may make the concept closer to a digital shadow than a fully integrated digital twin. Further clinical translation will require attention to verification, validation, uncertainty quantification, and the associated technical, ethical, and regulatory considerations.

papers.abstract: Vascular markers, lumen-like structures, and fluid-conducting channels provide evidence of vascular cell identity, structural organization, and channel patency, respectively, in bioprinted skin. A purposively assembled core of 19 primary or translational studies and 10 reviews informs the synthesis. We describe each vascular observation using independent fields for assay, compartment, endothelial source, observation time, model context, and construct relevance. Transient injection-assisted patency, sustained channel perfusion, and endothelial permeability are evaluated separately. Host angiogenesis, regional wound blood flow, and structural contact are distinguished from blood or circulating-tracer access localized to graft-associated vessels. Selected printed-skin studies demonstrate source-resolved host access in immunodeficient implantation models, whereas several transport principles come from skin chips or non-skin platforms. Four core studies treat newly excised wounds in diabetic animals; the clinical diabetic-foot-ulcer series has no vascular endpoint. These observations do not establish durable graft-specific vascular integration in clinical chronic ulcers. The review connects assay interpretation with bioink design and proposes product-specific reporting and validation priorities. Preserved search records and the core study registers are provided, while incomplete screening records, retrieval limits, and full-text availability constrain coverage. The synthesis is not a systematic review, meta-analysis, or estimate of evidence prevalence across the field. Clinical studies of chronic ulcers are needed to establish whether host blood reaches graft vessels and how long that access persists.

papers.title: Digital twin mapping model of CNC machining process based on sensor data stream sequence and graph neural network
papers.abstract: Based on the frequent switching of operating conditions in CNC machining, which can lead to step changes in sensor signal distribution, this paper considers the virtual real state mapping of the machining process as a frame level correspondence relationship and constructs a mapping model in which the physical side signal flow and virtual side state parameters interact along a directed graph. Secondly, the sensor channels form graph nodes, whose features combine window level time-domain statistics with wavelet packet band energy, and the directed coupling mask derived from the mechanical interactions between channel types fixes connectivity. Then, based on the standardized correlation between node features and the decoding state of the previous frame, this paper re evaluates the edge weights in each frame, where the coupling strength varies with changing conditions and the path set remains unchanged. The decoded parameters are re entered into the edge weight update of subsequent frames, and the loop between the virtual state and the graph structure is closed. The research results show that under the three parameter extreme value span switching sequence, the cutting force mapping error reaches 3.18N, the tool wear proxy error in lf determination under high-speed overload reaches 25m, and the median frame delay reaches 25m. The accuracy and latency behavior of the mapping are located in the constructed switching sequence, experience wear agent, and offline stream playback.

papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) in nuclear engineering offers significant potential for reactor-state prediction and digital twins; however, the "black-box" nature of data driven models limits their adoption in safety-critical, regulatory environments.This study addresses the critical gap in systematic sensitivity analysis and model-based interpretability for high-fidelity Pressurized Water Reactor (PWR) fuel-assembly neutronics simulations.We present a comprehensive 39-variable statistical and predictive assessment framework applied to a dataset of 24,360 simulation records, targeting the infinite multiplication factor (K) and the pin power peaking factor (PPPF).By integrating classical statistical methods with modern explainable AI (XAI) techniques including Multiple Linear Regression, HistGradientBoosting, Permutation Importance, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and Partial Dependence Plots (PDP) we evaluate how material and geometric parameters propagate to key neutronics responses.Results reveal distinct predictive structures: is predominantly linear (), whereas PPPF exhibits nonlinear characteristics best captured by ensemble methods ().Furthermore, a strong inverse correlation () and contrasting sensitivity directions between the two responses are identified, alongside response-specific predictive drivers.This research establishes a transparent, multi-tiered interpretability pipeline that bridges high fidelity neutronics simulation with physics informed insight, providing a foundational framework for multi objective reactor optimization and large scale uncertainty quantification.

papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) produces complex metal parts, but lack-of-fusion pores, keyhole pores and solidification cracks hinder certification. Acoustic emission (AE) provides complementary one-dimensional signals with microsecond-scale sampling and subsurface sensitivity. This PRISMA 2020 review searched ScienceDirect and OpenAlex through November 2026 for publications since 2015, with targeted searches and citation auditing. After deduplication, 2969 records were screened; 358 primary reports and 156 reviews were eligible, whereas 227 reports were not retrieved and two remained borderline. Within the 340-report expanded core, 282 (82.9%) address sensing or machine learning. A normal-incidence Ti-6Al-4V/argon model gives elastic-intensity transmission T ≈ 8 × 10−5; an idealised keyhole model illustrates resonance scaling. Reported spectral bands and material responses remain setup-specific; cross-powder-distribution accuracy decreased from 98.1% to 77.4% in one study. Detection is more mature than actuation, and most interventions are inter-layer. We define a 1 ms end-to-end intra-track latency as a design target, not a universal measured result, and propose an evidence-gated roadmap to autonomous repair. Scopus and Web of Science were not searched (no institutional access); OpenAlex is not an equivalent substitute, limiting corpus completeness.

papers.title: Lightweight and Interpretable ECAPA-TDNN for Neonatal Cry-Based Sepsis and RDS Screening: A Comparative Study of Spectral and Cepstral Features
papers.abstract: Sepsis and Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) are major neonatal health concerns for which non-invasive screening approaches warrant investigation. This study evaluates a task-specific lightweight Emphasized Channel Attention, Propagation and Aggregation Time Delay Neural Network (ECAPA-TDNN) for classifying neonatal cries into Healthy, Sepsis, and RDS categories. Following preprocessing and segmentation into expiratory cry segments (EXPs), Filter Bank energies (FBANKs), Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs), and Gammatone Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (GFCCs) were independently extracted and processed using lightweight ECAPA-TDNN configurations refined through architectural adaptation and Bayesian optimization. Classification was performed using a dual-dropout Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) head. On a balanced dataset of 8397EXPs from 51 newborns (17 per class), stratified 10-fold EXP-level cross-validation yielded overall accuracies of 97.23%, 97.18%, and 96.70% for FBANK, MFCC, and GFCC, respectively. Although FBANK achieved the highest mean accuracy, differences among the three representations were not statistically significant in exploratory fold-level testing. MFCC exhibited the lowest observed fold-to-fold variability in overall accuracy, while the corresponding FBANK, MFCC, and GFCC configurations contained 733,571, 707,939, and 687,635 trainable parameters, respectively. Integrated Gradients, t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding, and Squeeze-and-Excitation analyses provided complementary insights into model behavior. Supplementary interpretability controls supported the predictive relevance of selected features without establishing clinically validated acoustic markers. RDS exhibited the lowest class-wise recall, with recurring confusion involving Sepsis. Because newborn-disjoint partitions were not enforced, the reported performance does not establish generalization to unseen newborns. The study establishes an exploratory lightweight classification baseline, while subject-independent and external validation remain necessary before clinical application.

papers.title: Systematic validation and uncertainty quantification of SPARC90 pool scrubbing code against a qualified database
papers.abstract: Pool scrubbing is a passive mitigation system with huge potential for drastically reducing source term across diverse Severe Accident (SA) scenarios and reactor designs. Due to the wide variability of the governing thermal–hydraulic and physicochemical parameters, achieving accurate code predictions remains a significant challenge. This study presents a comprehensive and systematic validation of the SPARC90 code, which is the basis of pool scrubbing modules implemented in MELCOR, against an extensive database of over 100 “qualified for validation” experiments covering relevant SA Boundary Conditions (BC). The assessment also includes a systematic uncertainty quantification and an analysis of individual BC effects to check the code’s sensitivity to key parameters. The results indicate that SPARC90 generally captures global experimental trends, even though it tends to underpredict aerosol retention, yielding an overall Mean Relative Error (MRE) of −21 %. The code, initially developed for BWR suppression pool scenarios, show a good performance for flooded molten core interaction conditions (−12 % MRE). However, it systematically fails to reproduce experiments from specific scenarios such as steam generator tube rupture (−88 % MRE) and filtered containment venting system configurations (−95 % MRE), as expected from the lack of adequate models. An individual analysis of the code responses to governing boundary conditions demonstrates that it qualitatively follows expected physical trends. These findings identify specific modeling gaps and offer a structured framework to guide future developments in pool scrubbing codes.

papers.title: Modeling and Simulation of Model Predictive Control (MPC) and Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) for Enhanced Three-Axis Solar Tracking System
papers.abstract: Accurate solar tracking is essential for improving the utilization of solar radiation in photovoltaic systems. Conventional fixed-position solar panels cannot continuously maintain their orientation toward the Sun as its apparent position changes throughout the day. Solar tracking systems address this limitation by adjusting panel orientation according to the desired solar position. This study presents the modeling, simulation, and comparative analysis of proportional–integral–derivative (PID) control and model predictive control (MPC) for a three-axis solar tracking system. The proposed system consists of three independently controlled axes representing hour-angle, azimuth, and altitude movements. Each axis is driven by a DC motor represented by a third-order angular-position transfer function. The PID controller regulates position tracking using proportional, integral, and derivative actions, while MPC determines control inputs through receding-horizon optimization. Both control strategies are implemented in MATLAB/Simulink and evaluated under consistent simulation conditions. The proposed evaluation considers step-reference tracking, transient response, steady-state accuracy, and disturbance rejection. Performance indicators include rise time, settling time, percentage overshoot, tracking error, and integral absolute error. The study aims to identify the relative advantages and limitations of PID and MPC in three-axis solar tracking applications, with particular attention to tracking precision, control stability, and computational requirements.

papers.title: When Culture-Negative Prosthetic Joint Infection is Not Aseptic Loosening: An Unusual Presentation of Tropheryma whipplei Infection
papers.abstract: Whipple's disease, is a bacterial infection caused by Tropheryma whipplei , rarely presents as an isolated, culture-negative prosthetic joint infection (PJI), making diagnosis challenging and often delayed. We describe a 73-year-old man with a 12-month history of progressive left hip pain and unexplained weight loss following total hip replacement. Standard synovial fluid cultures were negative. Definitive diagnosis of PJI due to T. whipplei was achieved via 16S ribosomal ribonucleic acid polymerase chain reaction (rRNA PCR)testing of a preoperative hip aspirate. Systemic work-up showed no gastrointestinal or central nervous system involvement. The patient underwent successful single-stage revision total hip arthroplasty, followed by intravenous ceftriaxone and oral co-trimoxazole, with no recurrence to date. This case highlights the value of molecular diagnostics and multidisciplinary collaboration in diagnosing rare culture-negative PJI.

Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis perbandingan performa operasional tyre ukuran 24.00R35 pada Off-Highway Truck Caterpillar 773D, 773E, dan 775F antara periode inspeksi tyre konvensional dan periode implementasi Tyre Pressure Monitoring System di PT Cipta Kridatama site DMP, Sumatera Selatan. Empat parameter yang dievaluasi meliputi persentase kejadian low tyre pressure, service life, tread utilization rate (TUR), dan cost per hour (CPH). Data operasional dikumpulkan dari 35 unit alat angkut dengan 105 event tyre scrap pada tahun 2024 (konvensional) dan 91 event pada tahun 2025 (TPMS). Uji normalitas Kolmogorov-Smirnov menunjukkan distribusi data yang tidak normal pada sebagian besar variabel sehingga analisis dilakukan menggunakan Mann-Whitney U Test dengan Rank-Biserial Correlation sebagai ukuran effect size. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan perbedaan yang signifikan pada seluruh variabel (p < 0,001). Periode TPMS menunjukkan penurunan rata-rata low tyre pressure sebesar 6 poin persentase atau 86,7%, peningkatan rata-rata service life sebesar 1.312 jam atau 15,6%, peningkatan rata-rata tread utilization rate sebesar 9,9 poin persentase atau 15,9%, serta penurunan median cost per hour sebesar USD 0,26 per jam atau 22,6%. Temuan ini mengonfirmasi bahwa implementasi TPMS secara signifikan meningkatkan performa tyre dari aspek teknis maupun ekonomis, meskipun kondisi jalan tambang masih menjadi faktor pembatas dalam pencapaian target operasional perusahaan.

papers.title: Unsupervised Physics-Informed Neural Network for Distribution Line Parameter Identification Under AMI Measurement Conditions
papers.abstract: Estimating line resistance and reactance from advanced metering infrastructure (AMI) measurements is difficult when branch voltage drops are comparable to measurement noise. This study evaluates an unsupervised physics-informed neural network (uPINN) for impedance identification from voltage magnitudes and active and reactive power injections. The network uses power and voltage residuals and encourages consistent impedance estimates across operating snapshots. We compare the estimator with bounded linear least squares and an inverse power-flow baseline that uses nonlinear least squares on three radial feeder benchmarks under simulated measurement noise. The two baselines receive simulated voltage magnitudes at all retained buses, and the uPINN uses voltage measurements at metered buses. On the 118-bus feeder at a voltage noise standard deviation of 0.5%, uPINN yielded resistance and reactance mean absolute percentage errors (MAPEs) of 7.31% and 15.39%, compared with 15.02% and 31.40% for the inverse power-flow baseline. On the same feeder, the inverse power-flow baseline gave a lower reactance MAPE at the highest tested power measurement noise levels (2% for active power and 4% for reactive power). On the 69-bus equivalent, power flow calculations with impedances estimated at a voltage noise standard deviation of 0.2% gave a relative root-mean-square error in voltage magnitude of 0.0420%. The evaluation assumed known feeder topology and used impedance bounds derived from simulation references.

papers.title: Voltage-Secure Economic Dispatch of Active Distribution Networks Under Volatile Prices via Constrained Policy Optimization with Forecast-Augmented Observation
papers.abstract: The growing penetration of distributed renewable generation makes the net load of distribution networks variable and electricity prices volatile, so the economic dispatch of active distribution networks may violate voltage limits. This study aims to reduce the operating cost and carbon emissions of active distribution networks while keeping bus voltages within limits. The coordinated dispatch of battery energy storage, reactive power compensation, and diesel generation is formulated as a constrained Markov decision process, in which the voltage limits are imposed as a constraint so that voltage security takes priority over cost savings. Historical-average forecasts of the price, renewable output, and carbon intensity are included in the observation, and the policy is trained by constrained policy optimization (CPO). Case studies are conducted on the IEEE 33-bus and 69-bus networks. CPO saves 2702 and 2853 Chinese yuan (CNY) per day, respectively, the largest savings among the compared reinforcement learning methods. It also achieves the lowest carbon emissions without any voltage violation. The forecasts allow the policy to reserve stored energy for high-price hours, increasing the saving by 22% on the 33-bus network. CPO reaches 78% of the saving of model predictive control. These results indicate that, by treating voltage security as a constraint, the proposed method dispatches active distribution networks economically without violating voltage limits, supporting the low-carbon integration of renewable energy.

papers.title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network Approach to Nonlinear Suspended Sediment Dynamics in Open Channels
papers.abstract: Suspended sediment transport in open channels becomes a real challenge to model when concentration-dependent effects, such as hindered settling, introduce strong nonlinearities into the governing equations. In this study, a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework is developed to solve a two-dimensional steady advection–diffusion equation for suspended sediment motion that explicitly accounts for hindered settling. The formulation incorporates generalized boundary conditions at both the reference level and the free surface, along with sediment-free inflow conditions. In contrast to traditional numerical methods, the proposed approach does not need to generate a mesh and avoids the requirement for spatial discretization, while accurately formulating the solution to the nonlinear problem arising from the hindered settling mechanism. A limited but representative set of hyperparameter combinations is examined to understand the training behavior of the network, and a suitable configuration is selected for the present analysis. The proposed approach is made physically consistent by incorporating the governing equations and boundary conditions into the loss function, and robustness is achieved through the data loss term, where noisy synthetic data generated from the available analytical solution corresponding to a simplified subproblem are taken into consideration. The predicted values by the PINN are validated through both existing analytical solutions and experimental data sets available under specified flow conditions. The obtained relative L 2 error norm value of 2.82 × 10 − 2 demonstrates the reliability of the proposed framework while providing a physically meaningful solution for a highly nonlinear suspended sediment transport problem.

papers.title: Monte Carlo Simulation for Performance Prediction and Optimization of CdIn 2 Se 4 Solar Cells: Uncertainty Quantification and Parameter Sensitivity Analysis
papers.abstract: Considering its compositional flexibility, high absorption coefficient, and optimal direct bandgap (~1.7 eV), cadmium indium selenide (CdIn 2 Se 4) has emerged as a promising absorber for thin‐film photovoltaics. However, systematic device‐level investigations under realistic production conditions remain limited. In this study, we quantify uncertainties and predict the performance of Cu 2 O/CdIn 2 Se 4 /TiO 2 heterojunction solar cells using a Monte Carlo simulation framework. The simulation samples 5000 parameter combinations with physically realistic distributions, capturing interactions between material property uncertainties. Statistical analysis yields a mean power conversion efficiency of 19.8% with a standard deviation of 3.2%, while the optimal design achieves 21.91%, consistent with the literature‐benchmarked SCAPS‐1D model. Sensitivity analysis identifies defect density as the most critical parameter (importance: 34.2%), followed by absorber thickness (21.8%) and electron mobility (15.6%). Pareto frontier analysis reveals optimal efficiency–stability trade‐offs, with the optimal design (21.91%, stability ≈ 0.95) lying on the frontier. Yield analysis shows that 62% of devices exceed 18% efficiency, whereas only 12% achieve 21.91% under realistic tolerances. The top five parameters account for 88.3% of performance variation, providing clear guidance for experimental optimization. This work establishes a validated computational framework for predicting CdIn 2 Se 4 solar cell performance under realistic conditions.

papers.title: Adaptive Reduced-Order Kalman Filter with Parameter Drift Compensation for Sensorless Based MPPT in PV Boost Converters
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a sensorless output-voltage estimation method for photovoltaic (PV) boost converters using an adaptive reduced-order extended Kalman filter (AR-EKF) with parameter-drift compensation. The estimator is intended to support maximum power p oint tracking (MPPT) and other control tasks without requiring an output voltage sensor. The proposed method estimates the output voltage using only input voltage and input current measurements, eliminating the need for an output voltage sensor while maintaining high tracking accuracy. A notable feature of the proposed method is the extension of the state vector to include load resistance, which compensates for parameter variations that can significantly degrade estimation performance. The AR -EKF provides instantaneous estimation of both output voltage and load resistance, whi ch can be utilised in a model predictive control (MPC) algorithm to optimise the duty cycle selection for maximum power extraction. A comprehensive MATLAB simulation using converter parameters (85 kHz switching frequency, 0.86 mH inductor, 20 µF capacitor) demonstrates the method's effectiveness under varying duty ratios (10% to 70% drift). A hybrid-based observer is also implemented for comparison. The proposed method achieves high accuracy and a fast response, with an RMSE 0.0021 V, maximum error 0.0415 V, and a median settling time of 0.08 s, using only the input voltage and input current measurements. The hybrid observer achieves the same settling time but exhibits a higher RMSE and maximum error, while a conventional Kalman filter is significantly less accurate.

papers.title: An empirically evaluated online classroom framework for enhancing 21st-century competencies in higher education: a mixed-methods study
papers.abstract: Introduction This study develops and empirically evaluates an online classroom framework designed to support 21st-century competencies in higher education by integrating connectivism and social constructivism within a digital humanism paradigm. Addressing the limitations of passive, lecture-based virtual classrooms, the proposed framework incorporates retrieval-augmented artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots, real-time collaborative whiteboards, hierarchical mastery learning paths, and micro-credential digital badges to scaffold critical thinking, collaboration, creativity, and digital literacy. Methods Employing a four-phase exploratory sequential mixed-methods design, the study began with a contextual needs analysis involving 250 undergraduate students and 40 lecturers at a public university in Thailand, followed by system prototyping, expert design adequacy validation (n = 3), and a 16-week semester classroom pilot across two undergraduate database courses with two instructors and 100 students. Results In Phase 1, thematic analysis of qualitative reflections and multiple regression modeling indicated that online classroom environment structure (β = .421, p < .001), active learning activities (β = .385, p < .001), and technological support (β = .224, p < .001) significantly predicted perceived 21st-century competency support (R ² = .659, Adjusted R ² = .655, F(3, 286) = 184.24, p < .001, with consistent patterns across student and lecturer subsamples). In Phase 3, the web-based learning management system prototype achieved high expert adequacy ratings (22-item mean M = 4.64, SD = 0.34; domain-average mean M = 4.66). During the Phase 4 pilot, instructors reported high usability satisfaction (M = 4.95, SD = 0.07), and students reported favorable system usability (M = 4.29, SD = 0.52) alongside significant pre- to post-module quiz gains (54.2% to 78.4% on un-gated first attempts, d z = 1.99, p < .001; 84.6% on mastery-gated attempts, d z = 2.42) and behavioral telemetry engagement, supported by qualitative interview excerpts highlighting reduced learning anxiety and Socratic inquiry. Post-implementation multiple regression analysis indicated that nine learner experience predictors accounted for 86.01% of the variance in perceived content understanding (R ² = .8601, Adjusted R ² = .8461, F (9, 90) = 61.474, p < .001; process predictors alone R ² = .7351), with perceived academic achievement (β = .299), knowledge retention and application (β = .284), peer interaction (β = .231), and learning motivation (β = .149) emerging as significant positive predictors, while unscripted collaborative problem-solving exhibited a negative suppression weight (β = -.145, p = .017). Discussion The negative suppression pattern in unscripted group problem-solving may plausibly reflect collaborative cognitive load, coordination friction, or compensatory help-seeking. Overall, these findings offer an empirically grounded blueprint for transitioning higher education online courses into active learning ecosystems.
